competences: The learner identifies sourced facts about hiv/aids and population.
The learner explains information relating to Effects of HIV/AIDS on population and economic development.
languageCompetence: Pronounces, reads and spells: HIV, AIDS, population, disease.
objectives: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to state facts about hiv/aids and population.
By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to answer original sourced questions on Effects of HIV/AIDS on population and economic development.
priorKnowledge: Learners have already studied related ideas about Uganda and its population or government. They use this knowledge in studying hiv/aids and population.
materials: Reference chart about hiv/aids and population
P5 SST notes about Effects of HIV/AIDS on population and economic development
references: P.5 Social Studies Lesson Notes Term III: Uganda as an Independent Nation

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher asks learners to recall earlier Social Studies work and introduces hiv/aids and population. They ask the original question "State any two ways HIV/ AIDS affects economic development in an area." and note the learners' responses before teaching the content.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall the previous work, answer the opening question and explain what they already know about Uganda and its people.

steps.stage: Development: Meaning and key facts about hiv/aids and population
steps.content: C=Condom use. Social effects of HIV/AIDS on the population. It leads to many orphans due to deth of the parents. Economic effects of HIV/AIDS on population. He opened up Lugazi sugar factory MuljibhaiMadhivan Employing children as house maids. It provides relief aid in terms of food. How AIDS is spread. Through blood transfusion with an infected person. Use of ABC to prevent AIDS.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the sourced facts under "Meaning and key facts about hiv/aids and population", starting with "C=Condom use. Social effects of HIV/AIDS on the population.; It leads to many orphans due to deth of the parents. Economic effects of HIV/AIDS on population.". They explain the information, clarify the meanings and check learners' understanding through questioning.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source notes, explain the main points, answer their teacher's questions and copy the factual information into their books.

steps.content: State any two ways HIV/ AIDS affects economic development in an area. | Give any two ways TASO helps AIDS victims in Uganda. | How can married people safeguard themselves against AIDS? | What is population? | Write down any two advantages of a small population in a country.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher presents the exact sourced questions, beginning with "State any two ways HIV/ AIDS affects economic development in an area." and "Give any two ways TASO helps AIDS victims in Uganda.". They supervise the written responses, check the answers against the lesson notes and correct errors.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer the questions in their books, compare their work with the factual notes and correct wrong or incomplete answers.

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher reviews the important facts about hiv/aids and population and evaluates learning using "State any two ways HIV/ AIDS affects economic development in an area." and "Give any two ways TASO helps AIDS victims in Uganda.". They give guidance on the remaining original exercise for home revision.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer final oral questions, mention one important fact and make corrections in their notebooks before the lesson ends.

assessment: Use the original questions "State any two ways HIV/ AIDS affects economic development in an area." and "Give any two ways TASO helps AIDS victims in Uganda." and other exercises to test understanding. Mark answers and assist pupils to correct them using the source material.
homework: Answer the remaining original sourced exercise questions, especially "Which body in Uganda, carries out national population census?"
